typed.text: Automation task: automate the customer flow on the sandbox web pages with Playwright: create a customer on the customers page, check it appears in the list, then delete it. Today the customers page only lists customers: it has no form to create one, no way to delete one, and the list has no stable selectors. So the plan should propose a child feature task that adds a create form and a delete button per row to the customers page, with data-testid attributes on the form, the list rows and the buttons, as a needs-decision, before automating.

parentCreatedReply:
I've started TVMA33M "Playwright: create, list and delete a customer" as an automation task, and Jev put its plan step on Opus at high effort. The brief tells the plan step to stop with a needs-decision before writing any automation. That decision proposes a child feature task: a create form (name and VAT number) and a delete button on each row of the customers page, with data-testid on the form, its fields, the submit button, every row and every delete button, plus the routes, tests and a CHANGELOG line that requires. The proposal should name the actual test IDs and routes. I'll bring it to you when it arrives. If you approve, I'll create the child under TVMA33M and let the automation continue only once the child has landed into it.

The brief also has a full run use a throwaway SANDBOX_DATA_DIR, delete only the customer it created itself, have a --dry-run that stops before the create submit, and record video and screenshots for evidence.

One thing to weigh before you approve the child: create and delete is mostly the job of the project's own browser tests (playwright.config.ts and tests/ already exist). Once the form and buttons exist, a script in automations/ will largely repeat what the child feature's tests already cover. That's fine if a separately runnable flow is what you're after, and it's worth keeping in mind when the proposal comes in.

answers.question: The plan step has stopped with the child-feature proposal you asked for. It's solid, and I'd go with A. The child task would add `POST /customers` (fields `name` and `vat`, with an error message when either is empty) and `POST /customers/:id/delete`, both sending you back to `/customers`, using plain HTML forms and no JavaScript. The data-testids are `customer-form`, `customer-name`, `customer-vat`, `customer-submit`, `customer-form-error`, `customers-empty`, `customer-list`, `customer-row` (carrying `data-customer-id`) and `customer-delete`. The store in src/customers/index.ts already has create and remove, so it stays as it is. Tests and a CHANGELOG line are included. The automation that follows would start its own copy of the app with a temporary data folder, delete only the "Automation test <timestamp>" row it created, check that the list ends as it started, and save four screenshots and a video. The biggest thing in it you didn't ask for: it moves the request handling out of server.ts into a new src/web/app.ts so the routes can be unit-tested. That's a reasonable refactor, but it makes the change bigger, and TK46Z4X "Split the page rendering out of server.ts?" asked a similar question earlier today. Say so if you'd rather keep server.ts as it is. Against B: a confirm dialog needs JavaScript on a page that has none, and on a sandbox it buys little. C drops the create and delete you asked for. 1. TVMA33M "Playwright: create, list and delete a customer": A. Yes, as proposed...
